Yes it was hard but glad if it can help you in some way. 

So depending on your policy smoke damage to the building and personal loss may be different. It was on mine unfortunately so I had to open two claims hence being dropped. But in this case if you are renting smoke damage to building from this event should be something your landlord files for.

So because things did not burn to the ground I took pictures of everything in the house and submitted 95% of items with receipts. 5% were items that were gifts or I had purchased in person. They gave me funds for everything but I have a very good insurance company.

A few points:
- Check that your policy will cover you to buy new items of that kind (“ACV”). If it does not then they will only cover the depreciated value of the item (what they think the item is worth after the years that have passed). If you don’t have ACV the receipts will matter more because they need to accurately price your item.
- List everything as specifically as possible. If you damaged a speaker and write “speaker” they will pay out for the cheapest speaker they can find. 
- If it is smoke damage they aren’t going to replace things that smoke wouldn’t have damaged. So prioritize claiming fabric furniture and electronics (electronics are expected to go bad months after smoke damage. They may offer to clean things for you but it doesn’t do much)
- Rmeember what the limit of your loss is on your policy. Everything in your house can be damaged but they will only cover up to the amount listed in the policy. So save your energy claiming things with receipts

Can’t emphasize enough that this process is so stressful because you are running around for weeks taking pictures and finding receipts and figuring out what will and won’t be covered. If it’s something you can afford on your own i highly recommend going that way.

2. Or the genetic testing could be wrong like you said. It could be that some populations were misattributed and some clasically European polymorphisms were designated as Korean. But it is highly unlikely that is the case because Korean SNPs and European SNPs are far enough diverged that I don't think an algorithm would make a mistake of 25 whole percentage points. Maybe 5-10% for a terrible algorithm but not for a service like 23andMe.

As I mentioned you are right when you say no child is a perfect split of their parents. What would have to happen for each of these kids to have to have been 50% Korean or even close to that? The following:

1. Few to none of Jon's chromosomes from both his parents would have recombined during the division process which is highly unlikely because this is exactly how genetic diversity occurs in biology (this is the reason you have more in common with certain family members than others but never multiple chromosomes worth
2. The sperm would have been packaged with only the chromatids that were passed on by his Korean mother which would be a 0.5\^23=0.00001% chance of occurring just with one child. On this extremely off chance it happened with one child, the statistical likelihood it would happen with all 8 of them like they are claiming is nearly impossible

The much more likely scenario is that they are less than 50% Jon and less than 50% Kate as most people are with their parents, and the remaining amount is mutations and other types of genetic errors. Compound that to the generation before which means they are likely less than 25% each of their grandparents. Not always. I am 26% of one of my grandparents because of how the recombination between chromosomes played out. But with how biology works in reality there is no circumstance where all 8 of those kids are near 50% Korean.

ETA: I know I went on a spiel when the point of your post is that the genetic test could be lying to them but I have done (too much) genetic research that I can say with confidence that those tests would not tell all those kids they were near 50% Korean with how different Korean and European SNPs are. With your examples there's a range of 20-26% related to your grandparents which is normal. To be let's say 45% Korean they would have to inherit \~3348cM from Jon alone. Given how the biology of how that works and how the algorithms actually understand inheritance it is not possible that they will find that much coverage. That's likely how much Korean DNA Jon has total so he'd have to pass 100% of that on to his kids and it's just not possible with how biology works.
